_why: The collection baseline. A test module that stops being collected - a
missing optional dependency, a renamed file, an import error swallowed by a
skip - is otherwise invisible: the run still prints all-green.
These are MINIMUMS, deliberately. Adding tests must never break the gate;
losing them must always break it. Raise a number when a module grows enough
that the floor stops being meaningful.
Lower one only when tests are deliberately removed - the code they covered is
gone - and then in the same commit as the removal, whose message names the
tests and says why. Never lower one to make a run pass: a test that went
missing without anyone deciding so is the failure this file exists to catch,
and lowering the floor over it is the same move as editing a dataset to clear
Asserted by tests/test_environment.py under --strict-env only, because a
local run without the optional extras legitimately collects fewer.
